notes.he: שאם אמרו לו העדים נטמאת והוא אמר לא נטמאתי לא מודו ליה דנאמן:
notes.en: But with impurity: if the witnesses said to him, “You became impure,” and he said, “I did not become impure,” they do not concede to him that he is believed.

messages.text: What type of impurity are we dealing with? If we say
messages.quote: But with regard to ritual impurity, they do not concede to him

notes.he: באי זו טומאה לא מודו ליה:
notes.en: What are we dealing with: in which impurity do they not concede to him?

notes.he: במאי עסקינן באיזו טומאה לא מודו ליה אי נימא בטומאה ישנה מאי שנא חלבין וביאת מקדש כו':
notes.en: [In the other version:] What are we dealing with: in which impurity do they not concede to him? If we say old impurity, what is different about fats and entering the Temple, etc.

messages.text: that the baraita is referring to a case of old impurity, where the witnesses said to him: You became impure yesterday, what is different about the cases of eating forbidden fat and entering the Temple while impure, where the Rabbis concede to Rabbi Yehuda that one is not liable to bring a sin offering even though his denial is contradicted by two witnesses? He is exempt since if he wished, he could say: I did so intentionally.

notes.he: מאי שנא חלבין וביאת מקדש כדאמרן דמודו ליה דנאמן דאיכא למימר מיגו ולא מכחיש להו דאם רצה יאמר מזיד הייתי:
notes.en: [A printer’s marker: up to here belongs to 12a.] If we say old impurity, what is different about fats and entering the Temple, where, as we said, they concede to him that he is believed, since miggo can be said and he does not contradict them, for if he wished he could say “I was intentional”?

messages.text: Therefore, his denial can be interpreted to mean: My eating the forbidden fat or entering the Temple was not unwitting but intentional. If so, if he denies that he is in a state of old impurity, he can also explain his statement, since if he wished, he could say that he meant: I did not remain in my state of ritual impurity, but rather I immersed in a ritual bath.

notes.he: דאיכא למימר מיגו דאם רצה יאמר לא עמדתי כו' אלא ודאי בטומאה חדשה לא מודו ליה דליכא למימר מיגו וש"מ דטעמא דרבנן משום מיגו:
notes.en: With old impurity, too, his statement can be explained, since miggo can be said: if he wished he could say, “I did not remain, etc.” Rather, it must be that in new impurity they do not concede to him, since miggo cannot be said; and learn from it that the Rabbis’ reason is miggo.

notes.he: לא מודו ליה ור' יהודה סבר אפילו בטומאה חדשה אדם נאמן:
notes.en: [In the other version:] Rather, isn’t it with new impurity that they do not concede to him? And Rabbi Yehuda holds that even with new impurity a person is believed.

messages.text: Actually, the baraita can be referring to a case of old impurity, and nevertheless the Rabbis distinguish between one’s denial that he is impure and one’s denial that he ate or entered the Temple. The case is one where the witnesses say to him: You ate sacrificial meat while in a state of physical impurity, and he says to them: I did not become impure.

notes.he: טעמא משום מיגו בחלבין ובביאת מקדש איכא מיגו דלא נכנסתי שוגג אלא מזיד וגבי טומאה דלא מודו ליה משום דליכא מיגו ואע"ג דשייך ביה קרבן ואיכא טומאה ישנה דלית בה מיגו כגון אמרו לו אכלת קדשים כו':
notes.en: Ravina said: Actually: the reason is miggo. With fats and entering the Temple there is the miggo “I did not enter unwittingly, but intentionally”; and regarding impurity they do not concede to him because there is no miggo; and although an offering applies to it and it is old impurity, there is old impurity that has no miggo, for example where they said to him, “You ate sacred food, etc.”

notes.he: לא מודו ליה דאם (דחה) בטומאה חדשה אפי' ר' יהודה גופיה לא סבירא ליה דנאמן על עצמו דליכא למימר מיגו וכ"ש חכמים דלא סבירא להו דנאמן:
notes.en: Ravina said: Actually, it is in old impurity that they do not concede to him, for in new impurity even Rabbi Yehuda himself would not hold that he is credible about himself, since miggo cannot be said, and all the more so the Sages would not hold that he is believed.

notes.he: אלא במאי קאמר אבל בטומאה לא מודו ליה אפי' בטומאה ישנה קאמר אתמול [נטמאת] והיום אכלת קדשים. ובטומאה ישנה כי הא לא מודו ליה דלית בה מיגו כגון דאמרו ליה עדים אכלת קדשים בטומאה דנטמאת דחייב קרבן בשוגג ובמזיד כרת והוא אמר לא נטמאתי דהכא לא מתרץ דיבוריה למימר מיגו בלא הכחשה וליכא למימר לא עמדתי בטומאה אלא טבלתי:
notes.en: Rather, in what case does it say “but with impurity they do not concede to him”? It is said even of old impurity: “Yesterday [you became impure] and today you ate sacred food.” And with old impurity like this they do not concede to him, since it has no miggo: for example, where witnesses said to him, “You ate sacred food in impurity, since you had become impure,” for which he is liable to an offering if unwitting and to karet if intentional, and he said, “I did not become impure.” Here his statement cannot be explained by a miggo without contradiction, and he cannot say, “I did not remain in impurity, but immersed.”

notes.he: כלומר מאי דוחקיך דבטומאה חדשה מוקמת לה דלא מודו ליה משום דלית ביה מיגו אפי' בטומאה ישנה מצית למימר דלא מודו ליה ומשכחת לה דלית ביה מיגו כי האי גוונא כגון דקא אמרו ליה עדים אכלת קדשים כדאמר לעיל. ואמר לן ר' דלישנא קמא מיסתברא טפי:
notes.en: [In the other version:] Ravina said: Actually, old impurity. That is: what forces you to establish it as new impurity, where they do not concede to him because it has no miggo? Even with old impurity you can say that they do not concede to him, and you find a case of it with no miggo, like this: where the witnesses said to him, “You ate sacred food,” as was said above. And my teacher told us that the first version is more reasonable.

messages.text: The reason he is liable to bring an offering is that here he cannot explain his statement, as one cannot say that the phrase: I did not become impure, can be explained to mean: I did not remain in a state of impurity but rather I immersed.

notes.dh: ל"א מודים חכמים לר"י בחלבין ובביאת מקדש
notes.he: דשייך בהו קרבן אבל בטומאה גרידתא בלא ביאת מקדש דליכא קרבן לא מודו ליה:
notes.en: [Rashi now gives another version of the passage from 12a on:] Another version: The Sages concede to Rabbi Yehuda with fats and entering the Temple, which involve an offering; but with mere impurity, without entering the Temple, where there is no offering, they do not concede to him.

notes.he: ונגע בטהרות:
notes.en: With impurity: and he touched pure items.

notes.dh: ובמאי עסקינן אי בטומאה ישנה כו'
notes.he: אלא מדפסיק ותני דלא מודו ליה בשום טומאה שמע מינה טעמא לאו משום מיגו דהא בטומאה ישנה איכא מיגו אלא טעמא משום דאדם נאמן על עצמו הילכך היכא דאיכא קרבן הכי אבל בטומאה גרידתא לא:
notes.en: And what are we dealing with? If old impurity, etc.: rather, since it states without distinction that they do not concede to him with any impurity, learn from it that the reason is not miggo, for with old impurity there is a miggo; rather, the reason is that a person is credible about himself. Therefore, where there is an offering, it is so, but with mere impurity, it is not.

notes.he: טומאה עסקינן דליכא מיגו אי בטומאה ישנה האיכא מיגו ואמאי לא מודו ליה בישנה:
notes.en: And the Gemara asks: what impurity are we dealing with, where there is no miggo? If old impurity, there is a miggo, so why do they not concede to him with old impurity?

notes.he: איכא ישנה דלית בה מיגו וכגון דאמרו לו נטמאת אתמול ואכלת היום קדשים דהיינו טומאת הגוף ומתחייבת חטאת והוא אומר לא נטמאתי ואכחשינהו בין באכילה בין בנגיעה דלא אכל ולא נגע קדשים בטומאה ואי הדר ואמר השתא לא נטמאתי דקא אמינא לא עמדתי בטומאה לא קמכוין אלא למיפטר מקרבן (לא) ומאכילה דאית בה קרבן מכחיש להו מנגיעה לא מכחיש להו ואיתכחש דיבוריה קמא בטומאת מגע:
notes.en: Ravina said: Actually: there is old impurity that has no miggo, for example where they said to him, “You became impure yesterday and ate sacred food today,” which is bodily impurity, and you are liable to a sin offering; and he says, “I did not become impure,” contradicting them both about the eating and about the touching, [meaning] that he neither ate nor touched sacred food in impurity. And if he now goes back and says, “When I said ‘I did not become impure,’ I meant ‘I did not remain in impurity’,” he intends only to exempt himself from the offering: regarding the eating, which carries an offering, he contradicts them; regarding the touching, he does not contradict them; and his first statement is contradicted with regard to the impurity of contact.

messages.text: What would he say to them to explain his statement that he did not become impure? If he says: I immersed and I ate, then when he says this to them, his initial statement has been contradicted in any event with regard to his impurity imparted by contact. His initial claim that he did not become impure has not been adjusted with regard to this matter, and that claim was contradicted by the two witnesses.

notes.he: דמאי אמר להון אי אמר להון טבלתי ואכלתי כי אמר להו הכי איתכחש ליה דיבור קמייתא בטומאת מגע במה שנגע בטומאה. דהא כי אמר לא נטמאתי היינו משמע דלא נטמא כלל וכי הדר ואמר טבלתי מכלל דנטמא נמצא מוכחש דיבורו ראשון שאמר לא נטמאתי ואמאי לא מתרץ דיבוריה הכא כי ההוא דאמרו לו נטמאת בטומאה ישנה והוא אמר לא נטמאתי. דלא דמיא להכא. דהכא איהו לא קא מהדר להו במאי דקא אמרי ליה אינהו דאינהו קא אמרי ליה אכלת קדשים בטומאת הגוף ואיהו לא קא מהדר לא אכלתי אלא קא אמר לא נטמאתי היינו משמע לא נטמאתי [ממש] דהכא לא מתרץ דיבוריה כדאמרן הילכך בטומאה ישנה כי הא לא מודו ליה. ור' יהודה סבר אפי' בהא נאמן דמתרץ דיבוריה למימר לא עמדתי בטומאתי ולעולם טעמא משום מיגו:
notes.en: For what would he say to them? If he says to them, “I immersed and ate,” when he says this to them, his first statement is contradicted with regard to the impurity of contact, in that he touched impurity. For when he said “I did not become impure,” that means he did not become impure at all, and when he then says “I immersed,” it implies that he became impure; so his first statement, “I did not become impure,” is contradicted. And why can his statement not be explained here, as in the case where they said to him “You became impure” with old impurity and he said “I did not become impure”? Because that is not comparable to this: here he does not answer them about what they said to him. They tell him, “You ate sacred food in bodily impurity,” and he does not answer “I did not eat,” but says “I did not become impure,” which means “I did not become impure [at all],” so here his statement cannot be explained, as we said. Therefore, with old impurity like this they do not concede to him. And Rabbi Yehuda holds that even in this case he is believed, since his statement can be explained as “I did not remain in my impurity,” and actually the reason is miggo.

messages.text: The halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda that even if two witnesses testify that a person became impure, and he claims that he did not become impure, he is deemed credible about himself more than the testimony of one hundred people.

notes.dh: אמר רב נחמן אמר רב הלכה כר' יהודה
notes.he: דאדם נאמן על עצמו:
notes.en: Rav Naḥman said that Rav said: the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, that a person is credible about himself. [The daf’s text reads only: Rav Naḥman says.]

messages.text: Rabbi Yehuda said that he is deemed credible when he states that he is pure against the testimony of witnesses only when the person is by himself and only with regard to himself, but as far as others are concerned, he is regarded as impure.

notes.he: ר' יהודה שהוא נאמן וטהור אלא לאכול טהרות בינו ובין עצמו אבל לפני אחרים לא יאכל דלמא אתי לזלזולי בטהרות:
notes.en: He did not say: Rabbi Yehuda did not say that he is believed and pure, except to eat pure items by himself; but he should not eat in front of others, lest they come to treat pure items lightly.

notes.he: נאמן לאכול טהרות שהוא נוגע דאדם נאמן על עצמו אבל לאחרים לא יאכילם:
notes.en: With regard to himself: he is believed to eat the pure items that he touches, since a person is credible about himself; but he may not feed them to others.

notes.he: ר' יהודה דאדם נאמן על עצמו [אלא] בינו לבין עצמו ולעצמו כלומר אע"ג דנאמן דלא נטמא אינו רשאי לאכול בקדשים בפרהסיא אלא בצנעא בינו לבין עצמו ולעצמו ולא של אחרים:
notes.en: He did not say it: Rabbi Yehuda did not say that a person is credible about himself except by himself and with regard to himself. That is, although he is believed that he did not become impure, he may not eat sacred food in public, only in private, by himself, and with regard to himself, and not [the food] of others.

notes.he: ט"א ולעצמו רשאי להאכיל דהוא יודע (של עצמו) [בעצמו] דלא נטמא אבל לא לאחרים דדילמא אתי למימר בכל מקום אדם נאמן על עצמו יותר ממאה עדים:
notes.en: Another version: with regard to himself, he may eat [lit. “feed”], since he himself knows that he did not become impure; but not others, lest they come to say that everywhere a person is credible about himself more than one hundred witnesses.

messages.text: Although according to Rabbi Meir one is liable to bring an offering based on the testimony of two witnesses that he ate forbidden fat even if he denied it, Rabbi Meir concedes to the Rabbis that if two witnesses said to him: You engaged in sexual intercourse with an espoused maidservant, and he says: I did not engage in sexual intercourse, he is deemed credible, since if he wishes, he can say to them: I did not complete my act of intercourse, in which case, as stated earlier (10b), he is not liable to bring a guilt offering.

notes.he: אבל מיגו דמתניתין לא אמר דנוח לו לשקר לומר לא אכלתי מעשות רשע ולומר מזיד היה:
notes.en: Rabbi Meir concedes, etc.: but the miggo of the mishna he does not accept, since it is easier for him to lie and say “I did not eat” than to make himself wicked and say it was intentional.

notes.dh: דאי בעי אמר לא גמרתי ביאה
notes.he: שהעדים אין מעידין שראו כל המעשה אבל גבי חלב ראו כל המעשה אלא שלא היו יודעין מה היה בלבו ובנזיר נמי אע"פ שראו כל המעשה אפשר שמעולם לא הוי מוזהר משא"כ בחלב שהוא מוזהר ולענין עדות אפשר שלא היה בר הגדה שלא נתכוון להעיד וקרא כתיב והוא עד:
notes.en: Since if he wished he could say, “I did not complete the act of intercourse”: for the witnesses do not testify that they saw the whole act; but with forbidden fat they saw the whole act, only they did not know what was in his heart. And with the nazirite, too, although they saw the whole act, it is possible that he was never bound [by the prohibition], unlike forbidden fat, by which he is bound. And with regard to testimony, it is possible that he was not one bound to “tell” [Leviticus 5:1], since he did not intend to testify, and the verse states: “and he is a witness.”

notes.he: דנאמן על עצמו בשנים שאמרו לו בעלת שפחה כו':
notes.en: And Rabbi Meir concedes to the Sages: that he is credible about himself, where two said to him, “You had intercourse with an espoused maidservant, etc.”

notes.dh: מיגו דאי בעי אמר לא גמרתי ביאתי
notes.he: דאינו חייב אלא בשכבת זרע וזה אין מבורר לעדים ונמצא שעדותן אין עדות הילכך נאמן הוא לומר לא בעלתי: וכן בנזיר שאמרו לו נטמא למת וחייב אתה קרבן מיגו דאי בעי אמר להו אתם הייתם סבורים שהייתי אותה שעה נזיר ולא הייתי שכבר נשאלתי על נזירי לפני חכם או תנאי היה בלבי ולא נתקיים התנאי ונמצא שהעדות אינו עדות והלכך נאמן:
notes.en: Since if he wished he could say, “I did not complete my act of intercourse”: for he is liable only with emission of semen, and that is not clear to the witnesses, so their testimony is no testimony; therefore he is believed to say, “I did not have intercourse.” And likewise with the nazirite to whom they said, “You became impure through a corpse and you are liable to an offering”: since, if he wished, he could tell them, “You thought that I was a nazirite at that time, but I was not, for I had already requested release from my naziriteship before a Sage,” or “there was a condition in my heart and the condition was not fulfilled,” so the testimony is no testimony; therefore he is believed.

messages.text: Rabbi Meir concedes to the Rabbis in the case of an impure nazirite, i.e., one to whom two witnesses said: You became impure and are therefore liable to bring a sin offering, and he says: I did not become impure, that he is exempt, since if he wishes, he can say: I requested from a halakhic authority to dissolve my nazirite vow, and he dissolved it. Therefore, it was permitted for me to become impure. Nazirites are prohibited from becoming impure with the impurity imparted by a corpse, whereas non-nazirites may come into contact with a corpse.

notes.he: לחכם על נדרי ובהיתר נטמאתי והכי קאמינא לא נטמאתי בעודי בנדרי:
notes.en: I requested: from a Sage, regarding my vow, and I became impure when it was permitted; and this is what I meant: “I did not become impure while still under my vow.”

messages.text: Rabbi Meir concedes to the Rabbis that if two witnesses said to a person: You know testimony about so-and-so, and he says: I do not know, and he takes an oath to this effect, he is exempt from bringing an offering for taking a false oath of testimony. The reason is that if he wishes, he can say: I did witness the event, but I had not intended to offer testimony, in which case he is exempt from bringing an offering for taking a false oath of testimony.

notes.he: והוא השביעו ולא הודה וחייב אתה קרבן שבועת העדות מיגו דמצי למיפטר נפשיה בהיתרא ולומר מאי לא ידעתי דקאמינא לא נתכוונתי להיות עד:
notes.en: You know testimony: and he had him take an oath, and he did not admit, and [they say] you are liable to the offering for the oath of testimony: [he is exempt] by a miggo, since he could exempt himself in a permitted way and say, “What did I mean by ‘I do not know’? I meant that I did not intend to be a witness.”

notes.he: מכאן אמר רבי וכן דן הלכה למעשה דעדים ששמעו הדבר מפי בעלי מעשה אך לא נתכוונו להעיד ולא הובאו שם לשום עדות אין בעדותן כלום אם באים אחר זמן להעיד בפני ב"ד:
notes.en: I had not intended to testify: from here my teacher said, and so ruled in practice, that witnesses who heard a matter from the parties themselves but did not intend to testify, and were not brought there for any testimony, their testimony is worthless if they come later to testify before a court.

notes.he: וכן כשאמרו לו יודע אתה בעדות לפלוני שראית המעשה שראינו שהייתה שם ואם אי אתה מעיד לו חייב אתה קרבן על שמיעת קול אלה והוא אמר לא ידעתי פטור דאיבעי מצי אמר להון לא נתכוונתי לעדות לא שמתי דעתי להיות זוכר אם לאו הלכך אין עדותן עדות ונאמן הוא:
notes.en: And likewise when they said to him, “You know testimony for so-and-so, for you saw the event, as we saw that you were there, and if you do not testify for him you are liable to an offering for ‘hearing the voice of an oath’,” and he said, “I do not know,” he is exempt, since, if he wished, he could tell them, “I did not intend testimony; I did not set my mind to remember or not.” Therefore their testimony is no testimony, and he is believed.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches that if one unwittingly ate an olive-bulk of forbidden fat and then ate another olive-bulk of forbidden fat during one lapse of awareness, he is liable to bring only one sin offering.

notes.he: שני זיתי חלב:
notes.en: Fat and fat: two olive-bulks of forbidden fat.

notes.he: אכל כזית חלב וחזר ואכל כזית בהעלם אחד כיון דשם חלב אחד הוא אינו חייב אלא חטאת אחת אבל אכל כזית חלב וכזית דם ונותר ופיגול בהעלם אחד כיון דמינין הרבה אע"ג דבהעלם אחד חייב על כל אחת ואחת:
notes.en: He ate fat and fat: he ate an olive-bulk of forbidden fat and again ate an olive-bulk in one lapse of awareness; since it is one name, fat, he is liable only one sin offering. But if he ate an olive-bulk of fat and an olive-bulk of blood, notar and piggul in one lapse of awareness, since they are many types, even though it is in one lapse of awareness, he is liable for each and every one.

messages.text: Why is he liable to bring only one sin offering? But didn’t he eat two olive-bulks of forbidden fat?

One is liable to bring two sin offerings only when he ate the olive-bulks of forbidden fat during separate lapses of awareness, e.g., he ate forbidden fat when he was unaware that it was prohibited, and subsequently became aware of the prohibition and then forgot about it and ate another olive-bulk of forbidden fat. This is derived from the verse: “If his sin, which he has sinned, is known to him, then he shall bring for his offering a goat, a female without blemish, for his sin which he has sinned” (Leviticus 4:28). But here there is only one lapse of awareness.
messages.quote: Why is he liable to bring only one sin offering?

verse.he: אוֹ הוֹדַע אֵלָיו חַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא וְהֵבִיא קׇרְבָּנוֹ שְׂעִירַת עִזִּים תְּמִימָה נְקֵבָה עַל־חַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא׃
verse.en: or the sin of which they are guilty is made known—that person shall bring a female goat without blemish as an offering for the aforementioned sin.

notes.he: ה"ג העלמות מחלקין:
notes.en: This is the reading: “Lapses divide.”

messages.text: The reason that one is liable to bring only one sin offering for his two transgressions of eating forbidden fat is that both acts took place during one lapse of awareness; but if he ate forbidden fat in two lapses of awareness, he is liable to bring two sin offerings. But why? It is one category of prohibition of forbidden fat that he has violated, and therefore he should bring only one sin offering.
messages.lead: The Gemara cites a different version of the discussion between Rabbi Zeira and Abaye. There are those who claim that Rabbi Zeira raised his difficulty to Abaye in this manner:

messages.text: With regard to bringing sin offerings, separate lapses of awareness render him liable to bring multiple offerings.
messages.quote: It is one category of prohibition of forbidden fat

notes.he: היינו טעמא דחייב שתים דהעלמות מחלקין דאיכא שתי העלמות:
notes.en: Abaye said to him: this is the reason that he is liable two: lapses divide, and there are two lapses.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: If one ate forbidden fat, and blood, and piggul, and notar in one lapse of awareness, he is liable to bring a sin offering for each and every one of them. In a case where one ate half an olive-bulk and then ate another half olive-bulk during one lapse of awareness, if the two half olive-bulks were both from one type of forbidden food, he is liable to bring a sin offering. If they were from two types, he is exempt.

notes.he: שמצטרפין שני חצאי זיתים לחייבו:
notes.en: And a stringency with one type: that two half olive-bulks combine to render him liable.

notes.he: כזית אחד פטור שאין מצטרפין:
notes.en: From two types: one olive-bulk [from two types], exempt, since they do not combine.

messages.text: The ruling that if one ate two halves of an olive-bulk of one type of food he is liable to bring a sin offering is obvious, as he ate an olive-bulk of a forbidden food.

notes.he: אסיפא דמתניתין קאי דקתני שני חצאי זיתים ממין אחד חייב פשיטא:
notes.en: From one type, liable: this refers to the latter clause of the mishna, which teaches: two half olive-bulks from one type, liable. Obvious!

messages.text: This is referring to a case where he ate them from two dishes, and it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehoshua, who says that eating food from distinct dishes differentiates his acts of consumption and renders them separate transgressions.

notes.he: ורישא אכל חלב וחלב מיתוקמא בתמחוי אחד וחלב ופיגול ונותר נמי בתמחוי אחד חייב על כל אחד ואחד שהרי ג' שמות הן מיהו תימה אדמפליג בין חלב וחלב לחלב ופיגול ונותר לפלוג בחלב וחלב גופיה בין תמחוי א' לב' תמחויין ואיכא למימר משום דבעי למיתני סיפא זה חומר במין א' וכו' והא דתני זה חומר במינין הרבה כו' האי חומר משכחת לה נמי במין אחד כגון בב' תמחויין ומצי למימר דה"ק חומר במינין הרבה דלעולם חייב על כל אחד ואחד בין תמחוי אחד בין ב' תמחויין לאפוקי מין א' בתמחוי א' לא מחייב אלא חדא:
notes.en: Where he ate them in two dishes: and the first clause, “he ate fat and fat,” is established as one dish, and “fat, piggul and notar” also in one dish: he is liable for each one, since they are three names. But it is puzzling: rather than distinguishing between fat and fat and fat, piggul and notar, let it distinguish within fat and fat itself, between one dish and two dishes. One can say: because it wanted to teach in the latter clause, “this is a stringency with one type, etc.” And as for what it teaches, “this is a stringency with many types, etc.,” that stringency is found with one type too, for example in two dishes; one can say that it means: a stringency with many types, that he is always liable for each one, whether in one dish or two dishes, excluding one type in one dish, where he is liable only one.

notes.he: תבשילין חצי זית צלי וחצי זית מבושל:
notes.en: For example, where he ate the olive-bulk in two dishes: cooked dishes, half an olive-bulk roasted and half an olive-bulk boiled.

notes.he: איצטריך למימר חייב דאמר במתניתין תמחויין מחלקין לחטאות כדתנן אמר יהושע שמעתי באוכל כו':
notes.en: And according to Rabbi Yehoshua: it was necessary to say that he is liable, for he says in the mishna that dishes divide with regard to sin offerings, as we learned: “Rabbi Yehoshua said: I heard regarding one who eats, etc.”

messages.text: This ruling was necessary lest you say that when Rabbi Yehoshua says that separate dishes render his acts separate transgressions, it is no different if this principle results in a leniency and it is no different if it results in a stringency.
messages.quote: in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehoshua

notes.dh: מהו דתימא כי אמר ר' יהושע
notes.he: לקמן בהאי פירקא (שני חצאי זיתים ממין אחד חייב) תמחויין מחלקין:
notes.en: Lest you say that when Rabbi Yehoshua said: below in this chapter: dishes divide. [The printed Rashi has here, in parentheses, the words “two half olive-bulks from one type, liable.”]

notes.he: כגון אכל שני חצאי זיתים בשני תמחויין לא מצטרפין:
notes.en: Whether for leniency: for example, he ate two half olive-bulks in two dishes: they do not combine.

notes.he: דאם אכל שני זיתים בשני תמחויין בהעלם אחד חייב שתים קמ"ל ממין אחד חייב אפילו בשני תמחויין ולא פליג ר' יהושע:
notes.en: Or for stringency: that if he ate two olive-bulks in two dishes in one lapse of awareness, he is liable two. It teaches us that from one type he is liable, even in two dishes, and Rabbi Yehoshua does not disagree.

messages.text: Therefore, the mishna teaches us that if he ate two half olive-bulks from two dishes, he is liable to bring a sin offering. Evidently, Rabbi Yehoshua says that eating food from separate dishes renders his acts of consumption separate transgressions only when this principle produces a stringency, but he did not say it as a leniency.

notes.he: דלחומרא קאמר:
notes.en: It teaches us: that he said it for stringency.

notes.he: כדאמר ר' יהושע תמחויין מחלקין לא שנא לקולא לא שנא לחומרא דבמתניתין דמחלקין על כל אחד לחייבו מעילה היינו לחומרא והכא הוי קולא כזית אחד בב' תמחויין דאי אמרת דתמחויין מחלקין א"כ לא מצטרפי בהדדי לחייבו קמ"ל מתני' ממין אחד חייב אפי' בב' תמחויין אלמא לחומרא א"ר יהושע תמחויין מחלקין ולא לקולא:
notes.en: Lest you say: that when Rabbi Yehoshua said that dishes divide, there is no difference whether for leniency or for stringency. For in the mishna, where they divide so as to render him liable for each one, that is for stringency [the printed text adds here the word me’ila]; and here it would be a leniency, one olive-bulk in two dishes, for if you say that dishes divide, they do not combine to render him liable. The mishna teaches us “from one type, liable,” even in two dishes. Evidently Rabbi Yehoshua said that dishes divide for stringency, and not for leniency.

messages.text: There are those who say that this discussion referred to the latter clause of the mishna: In a case where one ate half an olive-bulk and then ate another half olive-bulk during one lapse of awareness, if they were from two types of food, he is exempt.
Isn’t that obvious, as he did not eat an entire olive-bulk of one type?

notes.he: ומדסיפא דאין מצטרפין מיירי במין אחד ושני תמחויין מכלל דרישא דקתני ממין אחד חייב דמצטרפין מין אחד ותמחוי אחד קאמר פשיטא:
notes.en: This is the reading: “From two types, exempt. Obvious!” And since the latter clause, where they do not combine, deals with one type and two dishes, by inference the first clause, which teaches “from one type, liable,” that they combine, means one type and one dish. Obvious!

notes.he: דלא מיצטרפי:
notes.en: From two types, exempt: obvious, since they do not combine.

messages.text: The mishna is referring to a case where he ate an olive-bulk of one type, but he ate it in two dishes, and it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehoshua, who says that eating food from separate dishes differentiates his acts of consumption and renders them separate transgressions.

This ruling was necessary lest you say that when Rabbi Yehoshua says that separate dishes render his acts separate transgressions, he says it only when it results in a stringency, but he does not say it when it results in a leniency. Therefore, the mishna teaches us that if he ate an olive-bulk from two types of food, he is exempt.
messages.quote: in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehoshua

messages.text: What does the mishna mean when it states the case of eating from two types of food? It is actually a case of two half olive-bulks from one type of food; and why does the tanna call it two types? It is because he ate it in two dishes, half an olive-bulk in each dish, and the mishna teaches that he is exempt. Evidently, it is no different if it results in a leniency and it is no different if it results in a stringency; in both cases Rabbi Yehoshua says that separate dishes render one’s acts of consumption separate transgressions.

notes.he: האי משני מינין מין אחד הוא ואמאי קרי ליה ב' מינין כגון שאכלו בב' תמחויין וקאמר אע"ג דמין אחד הוא כיון שאכלו בב' תמחויין תמחויין מחלקין ולא מצטרפין ופטור דלא שנא לקולא ולא שנא לחומרא קאמר דתמחויין מחלקין:
notes.en: Reish Lakish said: this “from two types” is one type; and why does it call it two types? For example, where he ate it in two dishes. And it says that although it is one type, since he ate it in two dishes, dishes divide and they do not combine, and he is exempt; for he says that dishes divide no matter whether for leniency or for stringency.

messages.text: From the fact that in the latter clause, when the mishna refers to two types of food it actually means one type of food but the case is where one ate it from two dishes, one can infer that when the former clause states that if one ate two half olive-bulks of one type of food he is liable to bring a sin offering, it must mean that it is one type of food and one ate it from one dish. But if so, why is it necessary to state this halakha; isn’t it obvious?

notes.dh: מדסיפא מין אחד ושני תמחויין כו'
notes.he: אבל לעיל דאוקי רישא במין אחד ושני תמחויין לא דייק מכלל דסיפא משני מינין שני מינין ממש כגון חלב ודם דאיכא למימר תנא סיפא אגב רישא אבל רישא אגב סיפא לא תנא:
notes.en: From the latter clause, one type and two dishes, etc.: but above, where it established the first clause as one type and two dishes, it did not infer that the latter clause, “from two types,” is literally two types, for example forbidden fat and blood, since one can say that the tanna taught the latter clause on account of the first clause, but he would not teach the first clause on account of the latter clause.

notes.he: כדאמרן מכלל דרישא דקתני ממין אחד חייב מין אחד ותמחוי אחד:
notes.en: And from the latter clause, one type and two dishes, as we said: by inference the first clause, which teaches “from one type, liable,” is one type and one dish.

messages.text: The mishna is referring to a case where he ate the two half olive-bulks but he had a period of awareness in the interim, e.g., he unwittingly ate half an olive-bulk of forbidden fat, then he became aware that he had done so, and subsequently he unwittingly ate another half an olive-bulk of forbidden fat.

notes.he: אכל חצי שיעור ונודע לא הויא ידיעה לחלק דאם חזר ואכל חצי שיעור מצטרפין:
notes.en: There is no awareness for a half-measure: he ate half a measure and became aware: it is not an awareness that divides, so that if he again ate half a measure, they combine.

notes.he: אמר רבינא הכא במאי עסקינן כגון שהיתה לו ידיעה בינתים. שנודע לו שאכל חצי זית חלב וחזר ואכל חצי זית בשוגג וקמ"ל אע"ג דהיתה לו ידיעה בינתים דלא אכלן בהעלם אחד חייב:
notes.en: Obvious that he is liable. Ravina said: What are we dealing with here? Where he had awareness in the interim: he became aware that he had eaten half an olive-bulk of forbidden fat, and again ate half an olive-bulk unwittingly. And it teaches us that although he had awareness in the interim, so that he did not eat them in one lapse of awareness, he is liable.

messages.text: And the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabban Gamliel, who says: There is no awareness for a half-measure. If one unwittingly performed a half-measure of a prohibited act and then became aware of his transgression, and then again unwittingly performed another half-measure of the prohibited act, his awareness in the interim does not prevent the two acts from combining. Accordingly, in the case here, it is as though he ate a full olive-bulk during one lapse of awareness.

notes.he: והא דקרי ליה העלם אחד לר"ג הוא דלא מחשב ידיעה לחצי שיעור ומכל מקום תני ליה לאשמועינן דאפילו בהעלם אחד משני מינין פטור:
notes.en: Who says there is no awareness for a half-measure: and it calls it one lapse of awareness according to Rabban Gamliel, who does not count awareness for a half-measure; and in any case it teaches it to inform us that even in one lapse of awareness, from two types he is exempt.

messages.text: As we learned in a mishna:

With regard to one who writes two letters on Shabbat, which is the minimum that one must write in order to be rendered liable for this prohibited labor, and he did so unwittingly in two separate lapses of awareness, one letter in the morning and one letter in the afternoon, Rabban Gamliel deems him liable to bring a sin offering for writing on Shabbat, and the Rabbis deem him exempt.

notes.he: הויא מלאכה בשבת:
notes.en: One who writes two letters: this is a [complete act of] labor on Shabbat.

notes.dh: ואליבא דרבן גמליאל דאמר אין ידיעה לחצי שיעור
notes.he: דההיא ידיעה דנודע לו בינתים לחצי שיעור לא חשיבא ידיעה לחלק השיעור דלא ליצטרפי לפוטרן אלא לא הויא ידיעה ומצטרפי כדתנן הכותב שתי אותיות בשבת דבהכי חייב בב' העלמות אחת שחרית ואחת ערבית דהיתה לו ידיעה בינתים רבן גמליאל מחייב כו':
notes.en: And according to Rabban Gamliel, who says there is no awareness for a half-measure: that awareness he had in the interim, for a half-measure, is not counted as awareness to divide the measure, so that they would not combine and he would be exempt; rather, it is not awareness, and they combine, as we learned: “One who writes two letters on Shabbat,” for in this case he is liable [even] in two lapses of awareness, one in the morning and one in the evening, where he had awareness in the interim: Rabban Gamliel deems him liable, etc.

messages.text: The basis of this dispute is that Rabban Gamliel holds that there is no awareness for a half-measure. Therefore, the fact that he became aware of his transgression after writing the first letter is of no significance. His awareness does not divide between the first act of writing a letter and the second act of writing a letter. And the Rabbis hold: There is awareness for a half-measure. Consequently, the two half-measures are considered to have been performed during separate lapses of awareness, and they do not combine to render him liable to bring a sin offering.

messages.caption: Bar Tutini’s two dishes in two versions: which clause of the mishna Reish Lakish explains, and what it shows about Rabbi Yehoshua; then Ravina’s answer for the first clause.

messages.text: Mishna
How much time can one expend while eating an olive-bulk of forbidden food and still be liable for violating the prohibition?

notes.he: לשני חצאי זיתים דאמר מצטרפין:
notes.en: Mishna. How much time can one who eats them expend: for the two half olive-bulks, which he said combine.

notes.dh: כמה ישהא האוכלו לאוכל כזית חלב או כזית דם או כזית נותר
notes.he: כלומר כמה ימשוך וישהא באכילתן שאעפ"כ נחשבת היא אכילה וחייב:
notes.en: How much time can one who eats an olive-bulk of forbidden fat, or an olive-bulk of blood, or an olive-bulk of notar expend: that is, how long may he draw out and extend his eating so that it still counts as eating and he is liable?

messages.text: The duration is calculated as though he were eating toasted grain, which one eats one kernel at a time. If he eats the olive-bulk of forbidden food within the amount of time it would take to eat an olive-bulk of toasted grain, he is liable. This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

notes.he: משערין אותן כאילו נתפררו לפירורין דקין כקליות ואוכלן אחת אחת וכשיעור אותה שהייה מצטרפים:
notes.en: As though he were eating toasted grain: they are measured as though they had been crumbled into fine crumbs, like toasted grain, and he eats them one by one; within the length of that delay, they combine.

notes.he: כלומר אפי' אם לקח כזית והפריש לפרורין ולקח כל פירור ופירור ואוכלו זה אחר זה כמי שהוא אוכל קליות גרגיר אחר גרגיר אעפ"כ כיון שגמר והשלים הזית הוי אכילה וחייב:
notes.en: As though he were eating toasted grain: that is, even if he took an olive-bulk and broke it into crumbs, and took each crumb and ate it one after the other, like one who eats toasted grain kernel after kernel, nevertheless, since he finished and completed the olive-bulk, it is an act of eating and he is liable.

messages.text: Unless the amount of time he expends from beginning to end is more than the time it takes to eat a half-loaf [peras] of bread, he is liable.

notes.he: מפרש בעירובין (דף פב:) ככר שהוא משלש לקב חציה לבית המנוגע. חצי ככר הוא פרס לשון פרוסה והוא ד' ביצים:
notes.en: Peras: explained in Eruvin (82b): a loaf of three to the kav, half of it for [the measure of] a house afflicted with leprosy. Half a loaf is a peras, from the word perusa [a slice], and it is four eggs[’-bulk].

notes.dh: מתחלה ועד סוף כדי אכילת פרס
notes.he: מהכא משמע דלתרי גווני מיירי שיעור פרס חדא לענין הפסקה שאם הפסיק בין אכילה לאכילה כשיעור פרס אין מצטרף וחדא כדאמרי' בעלמא (פסחים דף מד.) שאם נתן כזית תרומה בשיעור פרס דחולין ואכלן שהוא חייב עליה:
notes.en: From beginning to end, the time it takes to eat a half-loaf: from here it is implied that the measure of a peras applies in two ways. One is with regard to interruption: if he paused between one eating and the next for the length of a peras, it does not combine. The other is as we say elsewhere (Pesaḥim 44a): if he put an olive-bulk of teruma into a peras’ measure of non-sacred food and ate them, he is liable for it.

messages.text: Likewise, one who ate a quarter-loaf of ritually impure foods or drank a quarter-log of ritually impure liquids within the amount of time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread is rendered unfit to partake of teruma, the portion of the produce designated for priests, until he becomes pure.

notes.he: נפסל גופו מן התרומה אם אכל חצי פרס כדאמרינן בעירובין בפרק כיצד משתתפין (שם) וחצי חציה לפסול את הגויה:
notes.en: He ate impure foods: his body is disqualified from teruma if he ate half a peras, as we say in Eruvin, in the chapter Keitzad Mishtatfin (82b): “and half of its half to disqualify the body.”

notes.he: אית ספרים דגרסי שקצים ובטמאים מיירי וא"ת תיפוק ליה מכי נגע בהו טמא ויש לומר דתחב לו חבירו בבית הבליעה:
notes.en: Impure foods, etc.: some books read “creeping creatures,” and it deals with impure ones. And if you ask, derive [his impurity] from when he touched them: one can say that his fellow thrust it into his throat.

messages.text: Similarly, if one drank a quarter-log of wine and entered the Temple, and he remained there for the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, he is liable.

notes.he: ארביעית יין קמהדר דמשום אוכלין טמאין לא מחייב אביאת מקדש:
notes.en: Entered the Temple: this refers back to the quarter-log of wine, since for impure foods he is not liable for entering the Temple.

messages.text: If he interrupted his drinking of the quarter-log of wine or if he placed any amount of water into the wine, he is exempt.

notes.he: שלא שתה בבת אחת רביעית יין:
notes.en: If he interrupted in it: that he did not drink the quarter-log of wine at once.

messages.text: Gemara
Does Rabbi Meir state his opinion, that the duration of time is calculated as though one were eating toasted grain, as a stringency or does he state it as a leniency?
messages.lead: A dilemma was raised before the Sages:
messages.quote: as though he were eating toasted grain

messages.text: Does he state it as a stringency, and this is what he is teaching: The duration is calculated as though he were eating toasted grain a little at a time, and therefore even if it takes him the entire day to consume an olive-bulk of the forbiden food, and even though from beginning to end he expends more than the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, since he consumed a full olive-bulk in one extended act of eating, he is liable;

notes.he: כאילו אוכל קליות אחת אחת בסמוך זו לזו בההוא משערים שאם אכל כחצי זית והפסיק ולאחר אותה שעה אכל חצי זית אחר אף אם שהה מתחלה ועד סוף יותר מכדי אכילת פרס בסמוך זו לזו מצטרפין ואפילו הוי האי שיעורא כולי יומא:
notes.en: Gemara. As a stringency: as though eating toasted grain one by one, close to one another; by that they measure, so that if he ate as much as half an olive-bulk and paused, and after that time ate another half olive-bulk, even if from beginning to end he took longer than the time it takes to eat a peras, [eating] close to one another, they combine, and even if that measure is the whole day.

notes.he: זהו שיעור אכילה שחייב עד שישהא מתחילת אכילת הזית ועד סופו בכדי אכילת פרס: ר' מאיר לחומרא קאמר. דאע"ג דשוהה יותר מכדי אכילת פרס כיון דמשכיה אכילתו דאינו מפסיק בינתים ואפי' כולו יומא משיך בה הויא אכילה וחייב היינו לחומרא ואמרי לה רבנן כו':
notes.en: And the Rabbis say: this is the measure of eating for which he is liable: until he expends, from the start of eating the olive-bulk to its end, the time it takes to eat a half-loaf. Rabbi Meir says it as a stringency: even though he takes longer than the time it takes to eat a half-loaf, since he draws out his eating and does not interrupt in between, even if he draws it out the whole day, it is an act of eating and he is liable; that is the stringency. And the Rabbis say to him, etc.

messages.text: and the Rabbis said to him that unless he expends less than the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, he is liable, but if he expends more than the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, he is exempt?

notes.he: דבהא ס"ל כרבנן דבטפי מאכילת פרס לא מצטרף ולהכי מדמי לקליות דאם לא הפסיק בינתים אלא כאכילת קליות שדרכן לאוכלן זו סמוך לזו מצטרף ואם הפסיק לא מצטרף אפילו בכדי אכילת פרס:
notes.en: Or perhaps he says it as a leniency: for in this he holds like the Rabbis, that beyond the time it takes to eat a peras it does not combine; and that is why he compares it to toasted grain: if he did not pause in between, but [ate] as one eats toasted grain, which is eaten one right after another, it combines; and if he paused, it does not combine, even within the time it takes to eat a peras.

messages.text: Or perhaps Rabbi Meir says his opinion as a leniency, as this is what he is teaching: The duration is calculated as though he were eating toasted grain, which is eaten continuously one kernel after another, and therefore he is liable only if he did not interrupt at all in between his bites. But if he interrupted in between them, then although the duration from beginning to end was less than the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, he is exempt;

notes.he: כאילו אוכלן קליות זה אחר זה דלא יפסיק בהן ובעי נמי בכדי אכילת פרס אבל איפסיק ביני ביני אע"ג דמתחלה ועד סוף בכל אכילת פרס כיון דאיפסיק ביני ביני פטור:
notes.en: Or perhaps he says it as a leniency: as though eating toasted grain one after another, that he not interrupt between them, and it also requires the time it takes to eat a half-loaf; but if he interrupted in between, then even though from beginning to end it is within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf, since he interrupted in between, he is exempt.

messages.text: and the Rabbis said to him: Since the amount of time from beginning to end is less than the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, he is liable, despite the interruptions.
Come and hear the mishna: And the Rabbis say: Unless the amount of time he expends from beginning to end is the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread.
messages.quote: Unless the amount of time he expends from beginning to end

messages.text: Continues on 13a: the Gemara argues from the mishna’s wording, “unless he expends,” that Rabbi Meir issued his ruling as a stringency, and concludes that this is so.
